I had initially dropped this game for probably a year or more after having beat the game (aka, just one run).
I thought that I had gotten everything I could get out of the game. Until I started seeing footage of Hades II more recently and decided to give it another shot (just to see if I'd be remotely interested). 

Let me tell you! This game really is the GOAT for Rogue-Lites! You really just need to let the game breathe and evolve and you'll see that the game (and your character) grows over time. You start out struggling from room to room until you start regularly beating bosses and completing runs (with added difficulty settings!). The world is engaging with the best voice actors in the business for every line of dialogue. 

If you dropped this game or just wanted to try it out. I highly recommend it!

This game is absolutely amazing. The plot of the game is well written and interesting with great characters and dialogue. The design and aesthetic of the game is great and each new area felt refreshing and interesting. Each dungeon leaves you on your feet and the combat never gets stale or boring with the amount of variety in it. If you are up for a challenge, they have many options to increase the challenge to your liking as to keep challenging yourself and improving at the game. Learning the game felt natural with each run and meeting each new character was a great time. There is a lot about the game that I have still yet to experience but from the time I've sunk, Hades is an absolutely amazing game.

“Hades”, single-player, character-focused family drama. Like many great stories, its premise is simple. You are Zagreus, prince of the underworld, and for reasons yet to be discovered, he wants to leave his literal hell of a home. Hades, the temperamental father of “Zag,” is determined to impede his son’s escape by setting up a series of security checkpoints, that being said It's the first time I have ever played rogue-like genre, which means the player is expect to die over and over again, But it’s in death that the game’s narrative begins to sing.
This game has found the secret to (almost) eternal storytelling: a play loop that repeats itself, but dialogue that doesn’t. Interesting things happen all the time, in conversations and chance encounters as well as in battles, and no matter how long I spend with Hades I feel like I am only just getting acquainted with it.

The best part about the game is music, When I first met Eurydice, I genuinely just stood there listening to her sing for a very long while. It's beautiful, nostalgic and sad. This game is so good, the NPC really feel like people and I care about them. It's an endless odyssey.

if someone reading this is on the fence about buying it, I warmly recommend it.

P.S. Gonna have to try other games from Supergiant Games.

Hades is a hack and slash rogue-like game. Fluid controls, interesting story line with a decent learning curve. The problem with this game, however, is the repetitive like game play loop.

Your enjoyment with this game can be split into 3 sections without spoiling anything. First, completing the game once which your enjoyment is at the peak. Second, the repeating the same loop about 5 times with your enjoyment at its lowest, considering how you always see the same enemies. Lastly, the enjoyment for this game goes up after the story picks up the pace and you try to learn more about its story.

Overall, my experience with this game is positive but finding the motivation to continue playing was rather difficult especially around the 7th repetitive game play loop. If repetitive game play loop is a breaking point for you. This game is definitely not for you.

It’s been a while since I played it, but playing Hades 2 right now, I realized this deserved an overdue review! I really like mythology and therefore this game was already something to pique my interest and in the end the characters really made me like this game a lot. Talking to gods and other famous people from mythology in such a casual manner was so much fun, especially the way they are portrayed. Not only are they all so beautifully designed, they have their own personality making them fit, because I love games where not every ally is always nice or every enemy just plain evil. Anger, ego, quirkiness and even foes partially being funny enhances the immersion for me so much more.
The cast really pulls out the frustration if you fail a run or are annoyed by certain enemies. It’s also amazing how the dialogs don’t get repetitive after a while like in many other games where you exhaust them rather fast if you play a couple hours. It was such a joy with all these details to explore and getting to know these characters!

Great Music, Great roguelike gameplay with amazing replay value, interesting story, charming characters and Dialogue that is not only great but also doesn't repeat after even countless hours, what more could you ask for? Easily in my top 10 and possibly even top 5 favourite games of all time.

Super Giant Games made a repetitive and hard as nails task become something you can really enjoy, no matter where you come from. This is a game that has something for every kind of player, an interesting story, challenging gameplay, rewards that really make you feel like you are advancing something and not just upgrading numbers slightly, and more. Hades is a complete package, no other rogue like gets close to anything this gives you, and it beats almost anything 2020 threw at us. I rate Hades a 10 out of 10, much like any other reviewer, but for me this is a special verdict, Super Giant Games managed to make me enjoy an experience that I usually hate, enjoy repeating the same battles over and over just to see if Eurydice will forgive Orpheus or if Theseus will finally stop being a jerk.

This game makes a repetitive task seem different, and it's not just its awesome procedurally generated maps and encounters that make this magic happens, its Hades unique setting, story and delivery that makes each run feel unique. From your first fight with Megaera to your final showdown with the god of the Underworld, this game manages to keep you on your toes the whole way, with some breathing moments along the journey that only make it better.

I won't waste too many words: This game is perfect. Perfect difficulty curve and limitless playstyle potential. The art style is instantly iconic and Darren Korb's soundtrack is so good it actually feels unearthly. The ever-expanding world rewards you for every death with deeper relationships, new powers, and new challenges. Every run pulls you deeper into the story, and the story drives you toward attempt after attempt in a gameplay loop as ruthlessly efficient as the God of the Dead himself. And you just hate that guy, right?

Play this as soon as possible and prepare to lose track of time fighting your way to the Surface. Just remember: There Is No Escape.

Hades is a fantastic game that has received widespread praise and accolades for its engaging gameplay, rich storytelling, and lovable characters.

One of the standout features of Hades is its rogue-like elements, which add a layer of unpredictability and replayability to the game. Each time you play, the layout of the levels, enemy placements, and available power-ups are different, keeping things fresh and exciting.

The game's combat system is fast-paced and satisfying, with a wide range of weapons and abilities to choose from and upgrade. The various enemy types and bosses you encounter throughout the game provide a good challenge and require you to adapt your playstyle in order to defeat them.

But what really sets Hades apart is its narrative. The game is set in the underworld, and you play as Zagreus, the son of Hades, who is trying to escape the underworld and reach the surface. As you progress through the game, you'll encounter a cast of memorable characters, each with their own unique personality and story arc. The dialogue and voice acting are top-notch, and the relationships between the characters are well-written and engaging.

Overall, Hades is an exceptional game that offers a satisfying mix of action, storytelling, and replayability. It's a must-play for anyone who enjoys rogue-likes, action games, or just a good story.

Hades is a fun game for the first few hours and a chore after that.

Everything boils down to one problem - there is no meaningful randomity here. Sure each run is composed of randomly chosen maps, but they mostly play the same. Sure, there are about 40 types of enemies, but stunlocking is the best way to beat every single one of them. Sure there are different skills, but they all boil down to just changing some stat.

The final nail in the coffin is the system of permanent upgrades, persisting between runs. Instead of mechanics to learn there are stat bonuses to grind out. Progressing in this way feels empty, and with time kills any challenge the game presents.

I've played other roguelikes where each playthrough was set apart with different mechanics requiring different playstyles. Here it's always the same - just get in range of the enemy and smash the attack button until it dies (also dash a bit). It gets boring fast.

There is a nice story, good art, and music but they are all wasted on a tedious game loop.

This is truly a great game.

Individual runs are the perfect length for me. They always advance the plot and I absolutely loved the story.

Mechanically, the game is a lot of fun, and this is not my typical genre.

Just a great game overall!
